[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Configuration Management in Flask"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Effective configuration management is essential for building robust Flask applications. It allows developers to separate environment-specific settings, such as database credentials and debug flags, from the core application logic."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"The Flask Config Object"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Flask provides a built-in configuration object accessible via app.config. This object is actually a dictionary subclass, meaning you can manipulate configuration values using standard dictionary operations."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"from flask import Flask

app = Flask(__name__)
app.config['DEBUG'] = True
app.config['SECRET_KEY'] = 'your-secret-key-here'"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"Using Configuration Files"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"For larger applications, hardcoding configurations in your main application file is not recommended. Instead, you can load configurations from a separate Python file or object."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"# config.py
class Config:
    DEBUG = False
    TESTING = False
    DATABASE_URI = 'sqlite:///:memory:'

class DevelopmentConfig(Config):
    DEBUG = True

class ProductionConfig(Config):
    DATABASE_URI = 'postgresql://user:password@localhost/db'"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"To load this configuration into your Flask application, use the app.config.from_object() method:"},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"from flask import Flask
from config import DevelopmentConfig

app = Flask(__name__)
app.config.from_object(DevelopmentConfig)"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Environment Variables"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"Production environments often rely on environment variables for sensitive data. Flask can load configurations directly from environment variables using app.config.from_envvar() or by utilizing libraries like python-dotenv."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Never commit sensitive API keys or passwords directly to version control."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use distinct configuration classes for Development, Testing, and Production stages."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always ensure the SECRET_KEY is securely generated and kept hidden in production environments."}]
